tex_content.html:
Lemma
[A transversal orthogonal representative is the gradient]

↗ def:gradient ↗ lem:gradient-characterization

If $v\in T_pM$ is nonzero, $\langle v,v\rangle _g=df_p(v)$, and $\langle v,w\rangle _g=0$ for all $w\in \ker df_p$, then $v=\operatorname {grad}f|_p$.

Proof

\sketch Since $df_p(v)>0$, for arbitrary $w$ set $t=df_p(w)/df_p(v)$. Then $w-tv\in \ker df_p$, so orthogonality gives $\langle v,w\rangle _g=t\langle v,v\rangle _g=df_p(w)$, which characterizes the gradient.

□
